A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same Patronus work, and all supplied pages are readable. However, v1 includes Appendices A–D, whereas v2 ends after its references while still referring to an absent appendix. Main-text comparisons are reliable; judgments about supplementary material concern its absence from the supplied v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation, representation-quality, prototype manipulation, shortcut-learning and sensitivity experiments, including additional medical-image results in its appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original quantitative results in Tables 1–2 and qualitative reconstruction, manipulation, shortcut-learning and prototype-emergence experiments.

M1.justification: The prototype encoder, distance-based activation vector, conditional denoising objective, prototype manipulation, DDIM sampling and auxiliary latent diffusion procedure are retained. The new specification of a four-layer Conv–ReLU encoder documents implementation detail without establishing an architectural change.

E1.justification: All five datasets remain represented, but reported medical task coverage contracts substantially. v1 Appendix C.4 evaluates 23 CheXpert attributes covering demographics, health status, diseases and pacemaker presence, with attribute-directed interventions; v2 retains only qualitative CheXpert interpolation. The explicit cross-class interpolation scenarios in v1 Figure 20 are also absent.

E2.justification: DiffAE and InfoDiff, including the learned-z variant, remain the comparators in Tables 1–2. The published ResNet-50 comparison for CheXpert disease prediction in v1 Table 6 is absent from v2.

E3.justification: Substantive supplementary evaluation designs disappear: the 200-epoch CelebA sweeps over prototype counts and vector dimensions, and the binarized 23-attribute CheXpert probing protocol. Retained main experiments preserve five-fold logistic-regression evaluation, the AUROC capture threshold and FID evaluation over five sets of 10,000 images. These are omissions of reported protocols, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 omits the prototype-count/dimensionality sensitivity study, detailed attribute analyses, rare-pattern and cross-class interpolation failures, and extended age/gender reconstruction cases. The prototype-collapse experiment remains described, but its correlation distributions and visual comparisons in v1 Figure 10 are absent. Shortcut-learning evidence also loses its quantitative correlation analysis.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 9 identifies the temporal-emergence curves as means with standard-deviation shading over 100 samples. v2 Figure 4b retains the shaded curves without explaining the uncertainty bands or sample count. Main-table uncertainty reporting and five-set FID averaging remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All 50 mean-and-spread entries in Tables 1–2 are identical. However, v2 omits v1 Tables 4–6, including sensitivity results, individual CelebA attribute AUROCs and CheXpert results such as mean latent AUROC 0.74±0.01. Numerical shortcut-learning correlations and numerous qualitative findings also disappear; no comparable-setting performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: Section 3.5 substantially rewrites the proposition and proof. v1's likelihood-minus-ELBO case argument becomes an explicit conditional log-likelihood/ELBO/posterior-KL identity under a fixed forward process and an ELBO-improving update assumption. This improves the algebraic formulation, although the stated guarantee about generated versus data distributions remains stronger than the posterior-KL argument establishes.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain annotation-free prototype-conditioned diffusion, prototype visualization and semantic manipulation, competitive representation/generation quality, and diagnosis of unwanted correlations. v2 emphasizes temporal emergence more prominently, but v1 already claimed and demonstrated that capability.

C2.justification: v2 removes discussions of cross-modal interpretability, prototype-budget tradeoffs, rare-pattern and cross-class failures, medical interpretations and their qualifications, and the rationale for excluding ProtoPNet losses. It retains the global-feature limitation and adds a substantive proposal to use emergence timing for more efficient editing, counterfactual generation and potential bias mitigation.

D1.justification: v2 adds the four-layer Conv–ReLU encoder description but loses substantially more reproducibility information: Adam and learning-rate settings, dataset-specific input/patch/channel configurations, latent U-Net settings, and CheXpert preprocessing and splitting details from Appendix A and Table 3. The code-access URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: The central cited literature remains. Sections 2.1–2.2 sharpen comparisons with earlier prototype visualizers and explicitly contrast unsupervised intrinsic interpretability with post-hoc approaches. References supporting the omitted cross-modal and medical discussions disappear, but no new research lineage or fundamentally different positioning is introduced.

P1.justification: The document undergoes substantial condensation: the abstract is rewritten, related-work comparisons are expanded, DDIM equations are folded into prose, visualization and consistency explanations are merged, and diagnostic narration is shortened. The cross-modal discussion and entire appendix structure disappear, although the main section sequence remains.

P2.justification: The layout changes from two columns to one, and earlier illustrations are reorganized into four composite figures. Reconstruction, interpolation, extrapolation, prototype consistency and diagnostic panels are merged and selectively reduced. v1 Figure 10, the appendix figures and Tables 3–6 are absent; the two principal result tables remain.

improvement.justification: As supplied, v2 substantially weakens reproducibility and evidential support by omitting implementation details, sensitivity studies, quantitative medical evaluation and concrete failure analyses, while retaining references to an absent appendix. Main numerical results are unchanged. Clearer ELBO algebra and consolidated presentation provide limited benefits, but do not offset these losses; the revised proof still does not establish its broader distribution-quality guarantee.
